reviewedRevision: 60a3bca plus the rework in this commit
process: Lean final review at the user's request: the known 3-stage shortfall went straight to a retrofit, followed by one independent review round, one clean-worktree test run and a short browser check.
independentProbes: The reviewer's own reaction-limited bot, which reads only delayed public state and does not use the ferry model, cleared 160 of 160 crossings at both 0.25 s and 0.35 s (8 seeds, 60 Hz) and 119 of 120 at 30 and 120 Hz, and won 12 of 12 full 20-crossing campaigns. Thirty-seven blind patterns (idle, mash, random holds, hold-up, timed taps and alternations) cleared 0% of every crossing from 3. Turtles show a 1.2 s striped, arrowed warning before diving; hold-to-repeat hops every 0.32 s at every frame rate; Enter, Space and taps start a crossing from the select. Fuzz with hostile dt and pointer values, determinism at 30, 60 and 120 Hz, broken progress stores and EN/ZH text fit all passed.

findings.observation: Only 3 stages and no select or continue. There are now 20 data-driven crossings (teaching 1-7, combination 8-14, mastery 15-20) with logs, diving turtles, a cable ferry and trucks, each with a canvas cue and an accurate EN/ZH tip, plus a crossing select and env.progress continue.

An idle frog loses nothing in the first 20 s of crossing 1, only a short cue is drawn over the board, and the 1,149-line file is split into six modules with a quality test file covering per-crossing clears, blind bars, a reaction-limited bot, determinism, hostile input, broken stores and terminal state.

openNotes: Ferry crossings (6, 12, 17, 20) cause most lost frogs for a bot that extrapolates the ferry; players must read its slow-down at the ends.
Mastery crossings are only mildly harder than the middle ones, and the combination band is not harder than the teaching band.
Holding Up together with a side key gives no hop until one is released.
The select labels crossing 20 NEXT even after the whole river is won.

browser.method: Official Claude in Chrome extension, local server; real clicks on Start, Play again, the language switch and the touch buttons, synthetic in-page keys; only DOM text and the canvas were read.
observed: Chinese: Start opened crossing 1 of 20 (草地浅滩) with the cue drawn above the river and the frog clear; a tap of Up hopped one lane (score 10).
Chinese loss: hopping up blindly lost all four frogs and the loss screen advised waiting on the grass and watching the turtle arrows; Play again restarted crossing 1.

English 390 px phone frame (388 px inner, no horizontal overflow): the Up touch button hopped the frog (score 10); the long status line stays on one line (nowrap, 12 px) and is clipped rather than wrapping.
Not covered in the browser: a crossing win and the crossing select, which appears only after a first clear; the reviewer's bot and the quality tests cover both.
